videos.caption: Today, even the statue of Gautam Buddha was swept away by the devastating floods. A symbol of peace, compassion, and hope carried away by the force of nature. 💔🌊 This is not just a statue being washed away. It feels like a reminder of how powerless we can be when nature turns against us. Homes, roads, dreams, and now even symbols that have stood for peace for generations are being taken by the floodwaters, Nepal is hurting today. Behind every flood video is a family praying for safety, someone searching for their loved ones, and countless people watching everything they built disappear before their eyes. May everyone affected by this devastating flood be safe 🙏🇳🇵 May peace return to every place touched by these waters. 🕊️#NepalFlood #FloodInNepal #GautamBuddha #Buddha #Nepal

🚨 A 6-year-old girl was rescued alive after spending approximately 55 to 60 hours trapped beneath flood debris in Timure, Rasuwa District, Nepal. Members of Nepal’s Armed Police Force worked through mud and wreckage before reaching the child, identified in reports as Manisha, and safely pulling her from the destruction. 🙏 The girl received immediate medical assistance and was reportedly transferred to Kathmandu for further care. Information about her parents remained unclear following the rescue, which has become a powerful moment of hope amid the devastating floods that have claimed numerous lives across Nepal. #Nepal #Rasuwa #Rescue #Floods #SurvivalStory

videos.caption: Wildest Festival Yet 🤯🐮 Only in Nepal will you find a festival to do with people passing away, cows, dancing, cross dressing and loads more.  Welcome to Gai Jatra - which literally translates to cow festival.  There’s a huge historical story behind it which is too long to explain here but essentially people originally took cows through the street as a way of saying  final goodbye to their loved ones but now for practicality they use these giant effigies call Tahamacha.  Hospitality of Nepal is off to a fantastic start absolutely loving it here but it feels like there is a festival everyday in Nepal - full video on this will be out on the Youchooobz at some point.  #nepaltiktok #nepal #kathmandu #gaijatra

It’s already 2083 in Nepal 🇳🇵📅 Nepal’s official calendar, Bikram Sambat, runs almost 57 years ahead, and New Year lands in April. Even stranger: its months can be anywhere from 29 to 32 days long, and the lengths change every year because they follow the sun’s real path across the sky. No simple formula, so you need the new official calendar just to know how long the months are. What year would you rather live in?  #Nepal #Calendar #History #FunFacts #NepaliNewYear
